mainTopic: The claim 'give me my husband', whether קידושין money and gifts are returned when a betrothal ends, and the rules of שושבינות gifts.
overview: The גמרא asks why the one who received שושבינות gifts can't say 'give me my groomsman', the way a betrothed woman can say 'give me my husband'. רב יוסף answers that the seven days of rejoicing already took place, so the debt is already owed. The גמרא then asks whether the claim 'give me my husband' is a dispute between תנאים, using a ברייתא of רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא. It concludes that everyone accepts the claim. The real argument is whether קידושין money is given to be kept for good (לטיבועין). A second ברייתא with רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי is explained as the same argument, about a כהן's betrothed who was forced; רבי יוסי splits the money because he is unsure. The אמוראים then rule in practice: gifts come back but the קידושין money does not, unless she backs out. אמימר holds the קידושין money is never returned, so people won't think he may marry her sister, and the גמרא rejects רב אשי's answer to this. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה and begins a ברייתא listing five rules about שושבינות, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why can't he say "Give me my groomsman"?
steps.stepSummary: Based on שמואל's ruling that a betrothed woman may say "give me my husband," the גמרא asks why the one who got שושבינות gifts can't say "give me my groomsman."
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said a woman can claim, "Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him." Here too, let him say, "Give me my groomsman and I will rejoice with him!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling about שושבינות. It uses another ruling of his: a betrothed woman can say "give me my husband," meaning "it's not my fault the wedding didn't happen."
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל lets the woman keep the קידושין money because she was ready to go through with the wedding. The same logic should help the one who got the gifts: "I was ready to rejoice with my groomsman and pay him back, but he died." So why does he still have to repay?

keyTerms.meaning: "Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him": a claim that it's not my fault the wedding didn't happen
Groomsman: a friend who gives gifts at a wedding and expects the same back at his own wedding
Here too: the same logic should apply in this case

phrases.english: "Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him."
phrases.notes: This is the end of a quote from שמואל: the woman keeps the קידושין money, since she was ready to marry.

phrases.english: Here too, let him say:
"Give me my groomsman and I will rejoice with him!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling about שושבינות, which came just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that שושבינות must still be repaid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל accepts "it's not my fault" for the betrothed woman. The same claim should then free the gift-receiver from repaying.
steps.whyThisMatters: It tests whether "I was ready but the other side couldn't go through with it" is a general rule or limited to its case.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the rejoicing already happened
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that שמואל's case is where the seven days of rejoicing already took place, but the repayment wasn't made before the man died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Here we are dealing with a case where he already rejoiced with him for the seven days of the feast, but did not manage to repay him before he died.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by narrowing שמואל's case. In his case the celebrating was already finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim "give me my groomsman" only works if the rejoicing never happened. Here it did happen for all seven days, so the debt was already set. The person simply didn't pay before the death.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a ruling to a specific case)
The seven days of the wedding feast
To repay him

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
With what are we dealing here?

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁשָּׂמַח עִמּוֹ שִׁבְעָה יְמֵי מִשְׁתֶּה,
phrases.english: Where he rejoiced with him the seven days of the feast,
and did not manage to repay him before he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the rejoicing never happened, so "give me my groomsman" should work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rejoicing did happen, so the debt is fixed and the claim doesn't apply.
steps.whatToRemember: "Give me my husband/groomsman" only helps when the celebration never took place. Once it took place, the obligation stands.

steps.title: Is "Give me my husband" a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's claim is debated by תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא about returning קידושין money where רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that "Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him" is a dispute between תנאים? For it was taught: One who betroths a woman: a virgin collects two hundred, a widow one hundred. Where the custom is to return the קידושין money, they return it. Where the custom is not to return it, they don't. These are the words of רבי נתן. רבי יהודה הנשיא says: In truth they said: Where the custom is to return it, they return it. Where the custom is not to return it, they don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new line of questioning: maybe שמואל's idea is actually argued over by תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא to set up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא deals with a betrothal that ended before the wedding. The question is whether the קידושין money goes back, and the answer depends on local custom. The two opinions are quoted side by side, and the next step will point out a problem with them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
One who betroths (does אירוסין)
A מנה, equal to one hundred דינרים
A place where the custom is
"In truth they said": introduces a firm, set rule

phrases.english: Shall we say that "Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him"
is a dispute of תנאים?
As it was taught: One who betroths a woman;
a virgin collects two hundred,
phrases.notes: Two hundred דינרים: her כתובה money, which she collects even though they were only betrothed.

phrases.english: and a widow, one hundred.
A place where they were accustomed to return the betrothal money, they return it;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַחְזִיר קִדּוּשִׁין – אֵין מַחְזִירִין,
phrases.english: a place where they were accustomed not to return the betrothal money, they do not return it.
These are the words of Rabbi Natan.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא אוֹמֵר, בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: In truth they said:
A place where they were accustomed to return, they return;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַחְזִיר – אֵין מַחְזִירִין.
phrases.english: a place where they were accustomed not to return, they do not return.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending שמואל, the גמרא opens a new question about the source of his claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the claim "give me my husband" a matter of dispute between תנאים?
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא about returning קידושין money.

steps.title: The two opinions sound the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי יהודה הנשיא seems to say exactly what the תנא קמא (רבי נתן) said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא is the same as the first תנא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that both opinions in the ברייתא use the same words. This sets up the next move: finding the hidden difference between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא wouldn't quote two תנאים as arguing if they agree completely. So there must be some real difference between them that isn't stated outright.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
The first תנא: the first opinion quoted

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא!
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's presentation of two opinions as a dispute.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions have the same wording, so it looks like there is no dispute at all.

steps.title: Maybe they argue about "Give me my husband"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the real difference between the two תנאים is whether the claim "give me my husband" is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that the difference between them is the claim "Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes the hidden difference: the two תנאים argue about whether the woman's claim "give me my husband" works. The sentence ends with a dash, so the discussion continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this is right, then שמואל's ruling is a debated point between תנאים, not something everyone agrees on. That is exactly what the question in step 3 suggested.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that: proposes the only reasonable explanation
There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: This is still a suggestion ("is it not...?"), not the final answer. The גמרא rejects it in step 8.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו ״תְּנוּ לִי בַּעְלִי וְאֶשְׂמַח עִמּוֹ״
phrases.english: Rather, is it not that "Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him"
is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from step 4 by finding a difference between the תנאים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two תנאים differ over whether "give me my husband" is a valid claim. That would make שמואל's ruling a dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: Filling in the missing words of the ברייתא: רבי נתן's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא is missing words and rewrites רבי נתן's view. If she died, local custom decides whether the money is returned. If he died, it is never returned, because she can say 'give me my husband'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is missing words, and this is what it means. A betrothed virgin collects two hundred and a widow one hundred. That applies when he backed out. If she died, it depends on local custom. That is only when she died. If he died, nothing is returned, because she can say: 'Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is building out the suggestion from the previous step by rewriting the ברייתא with its missing words added, so we can see exactly what רבי נתן holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי נתן splits the death cases. If she died, local custom decides. If he died, the money is never returned, because the woman was ready to marry and is not at fault. This sets up the contrast with רבי יהודה הנשיא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is missing words.' The גמרא fills in words it says are missing from the text.
One who betroths (does אירוסין / קידושין)
A מנה, one hundred זוז; the widow's כתובה amount
A place where people have a set custom

steps.confusionAlert: This is still only a suggestion. The גמרא will reject this way of reading the dispute in step 8.

phrases.english: And it is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
One who betroths a woman,
if she is a virgin, she collects two hundred,
and if a widow, a maneh.
In what case are these words said?
Where he backed out;
but if she died,
in a place where they are accustomed to return, they return;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַחְזִיר, אֵין מַחְזִירִין.
phrases.english: in a place where they are accustomed not to return, they do not return.
And this is only where she died,
but if he died, they do not return.
What is the reason?
She can say:
'Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the proposed answer from step 5 by rewriting the ברייתא with missing words added.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי נתן, when the man died the money is never returned, because of the claim 'give me my husband'. When she died, local custom decides.

steps.title: Filling in the missing words: רבי יהודה הנשיא's view
steps.stepSummary: In the rewritten ברייתא, רבי יהודה הנשיא says local custom decides whether he died or she died. On this reading, he does not accept the claim 'give me my husband'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא came to say: Really they said that whether he died or she died, local custom decides. Where they return, they return. Where they don't, they don't. And she cannot say 'Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The rewrite continues. Now רבי יהודה הנשיא is shown disagreeing with רבי נתן by treating both deaths the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This now gives רבי יהודה הנשיא a real new point, which answers the problem from step 4. רבי נתן said the money is never returned when he dies. רבי יהודה הנשיא says custom decides even then, because he rejects her claim. So on this reading, the dispute is exactly about שמואל's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Truly they said.' A phrase that introduces a firm, settled rule.
She is not able to claim

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה הנשיא came to say:
Truly they said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מֵת הוּא, וּבֵין מֵתָה הִיא;
phrases.english: whether he died or she died,
in a place where they are accustomed to return, they return;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַחְזִיר – אֵין מַחְזִירִין;
phrases.english: in a place where they are accustomed not to return, they do not return;
and she cannot say:
'Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rewritten ברייתא by giving רבי יהודה הנשיא's opposing view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה הנשיא rejects the claim 'give me my husband', so custom decides even when the man died. This would make the claim a debate between תנאים.

steps.title: Everyone accepts her claim; the real dispute is whether קידושין money is meant to be kept
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reading above. Everyone agrees she can say 'give me my husband', so if he died, nothing is returned. They argue only when she died. The question is whether קידושין money is given to be kept for good (לטיבועין).
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees she can say 'Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him.' When he died, nobody argues. They argue only when she died. The question is whether קידושין money is given to be 'sunk', never coming back. רבי נתן says it is not, so custom decides. רבי יהודה הנשיא says it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the whole suggestion. It says the two תנאים do not argue about שמואל's claim at all, and it gives a different reason for their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So שמואל's claim is not a debate between תנאים; everyone accepts it. The argument moves to the case where she died. רבי נתן says the money was not given to be kept no matter what, so local custom of returning applies. רבי יהודה הנשיא says it was, so the קידושין money is never returned.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone (both תנאים agree)
They argue
Given to be 'sunk'. The money is the receiver's for good and never comes back.

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves שמואל's claim from being a debate between תנאים. Now everyone holds she can say 'give me my husband'.

phrases.english: No; everyone agrees she can say:
'Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him.'

phrases.aramaic: וּדְמִית הוּא – כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: And where he died, everyone agrees,
where they argue is where she died;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין לְטִיבּוּעִין נִיתְּנוּ קָא מִיפַּלְגִי –
phrases.english: and here they argue about whether קידושין money is given to be 'sunk':
רבי נתן holds:
קידושין money is not given to be sunk,
and רבי יהודה הנשיא holds:
קידושין money is given to be sunk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading in steps 5-7 and gives a new reason for the dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the תנאים argue about the claim 'give me my husband'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained another way, as an argument over whether קידושין money is given to be kept for good. So the claim itself can be held by everyone.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה הנשיא mentions a custom of returning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new explanation. If רבי יהודה הנשיא holds that קידושין money is never returned, why does he say that where the custom is to return, they return?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches, in רבי יהודה הנשיא's words, 'In a place where they are accustomed to return, they return'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation it just gave, pointing to words in רבי יהודה הנשיא's own statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is given to be kept for good should never be returned, whatever the custom. Yet רבי יהודה הנשיא speaks of places that return. That seems to contradict the idea that he holds קידושין money is לטיבועין.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it teaches.' Used to quote back a line of a text that seems to contradict what was just said.

phrases.english: But 'in a place where they are accustomed to return,
they return' is taught!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of רבי יהודה הנשיא's view given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה הנשיא holds קידושין money is לטיבועין ניתנו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the money is never returned, a custom of returning should not matter. But his own words mention it.

steps.title: He is talking about the presents, not the קידושין money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה הנשיא's mention of returning is about the presents (סבלונות) the groom sent. Those are returned where that is the custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: the presents, certainly, in a place where they are accustomed to return them, they are returned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its explanation by saying the line about returning refers to a different thing: the gifts, not the קידושין money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, רבי יהודה הנשיא holds that the קידושין money itself is never returned. The extra gifts the groom sent after the קידושין follow local custom. So the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what he means.' Used to explain a statement in a new way.
Presents the groom sends his betrothed after the קידושין

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, everyone accepts the claim 'give me my husband', so when he dies nothing is returned. When she dies, רבי נתן says custom decides about the קידושין money. רבי יהודה הנשיא says the קידושין money is never returned, and only the סבלונות follow custom.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
and the presents, certainly,
in a place where they are accustomed to return, they return.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by explaining what the words about returning refer to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the line is about a different thing (the presents)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words about returning refer to the קידושין money, which would contradict לטיבועין ניתנו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words refer to the סבלונות. The קידושין money itself is never returned according to רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.title: A second ברייתא with the same kind of dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the earlier dispute matches another dispute in a ברייתא. It then quotes that ברייתא: a man betrothed a woman with a כיכר of silver. רבי מאיר says she collects her כתובה on top of it. רבי יהודה says she collects her כתובה and returns the rest. רבי יוסי gives puzzling numbers.
steps.simpleTranslation: These תנאים argue the same way as those תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: if he betrothed her with a כיכר of silver, a virgin collects 200 and a widow collects a מנה (100). This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says a virgin collects 200 and a widow a מנה, and she gives him back the rest. רבי יוסי says: if he betrothed her with 20, he gives her 30 halves. If he betrothed her with 30, he gives her 20 halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new source. It brings a ברייתא where תנאים argue the same question we just saw: does the woman keep the קידושין money?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the dispute was about whether קידושין money is given לטיבועין, to be kept for good. Here רבי מאיר lets her keep the huge קידושין gift and still collect her כתובה. רבי יהודה makes her return whatever is beyond her כתובה. רבי יוסי's numbers are not explained yet; the גמרא will explain them in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: A talent, a very large weight of silver
Collects (her כתובה money)
One hundred דינרים, the basic כתובה of a widow
She gives him back the rest
Halves, meaning half-סלעים

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי's numbers look backwards: more קידושין money, yet she gets less. Don't try to solve it yet. The גמרא explains it in step 16.

phrases.english: And these tannaim are like those tannaim,
phrases.notes: He means the dispute coming up matches the dispute we just discussed about returning קידושין money.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:
If he betrothed her with a talent of silver,
a virgin collects two hundred,
and a widow a maneh (one hundred);
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּתוּלָה גּוֹבָה מָאתַיִם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: A virgin collects two hundred,
and a widow a maneh;
and she returns the rest to him.
Rabbi Yosei says: If he betrothed her with twenty,
he gives her thirty halves.
If he betrothed her with thirty,
he gives her twenty halves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא to the dispute just explained in steps 8-10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: she keeps the קידושין money and also collects her כתובה. רבי יהודה: she collects her כתובה and returns the rest. רבי יוסי: puzzling half amounts.

steps.title: What case is this ברייתא about? Not if she died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation the ברייתא is talking about. It cannot be that she died, because a dead woman does not collect a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say she died, does she get a כתובה at all?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts looking for the case the ברייתא must mean. It tests the first option, that the woman died, and throws it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks about her collecting a כתובה. A כתובה is paid to the wife when the marriage ends by his death or by divorce. If she died, there is no כתובה to collect, so this option fails.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say (first suggestion)
The money a wife collects when the marriage ends

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If we say that she died,
does she have a ketubah?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case the newly quoted ברייתא is about
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What situation the ברייתא is discussing, such that she collects a כתובה and the קידושין money is in question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not if she died, since then she has no כתובה

steps.title: Not if he died either
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the husband died. But then why would רבי יהודה make her return the rest? She can say 'give me my husband and I will be happy with him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe he died. Then why does she give him back the rest? Let her say: 'Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second option, that the husband died, and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As step 8 said, everyone agrees that when he dies she can claim 'give me my husband'. She did not break the deal; she was ready to marry him. So she would keep everything, and רבי יהודה's ruling that she returns the rest would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him: she was ready, so she is not at fault
Why?

phrases.english: Rather, that he died,
why does she return the rest to him?
Let her say: "Give me my husband and I will rejoice with him!"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא שֶׁמֵּת הוּא אַמַּאי מַחְזֶרֶת לוֹ אֶת הַשְּׁאָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second suggestion after the first was rejected
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the ברייתא is about the husband's death
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If he died she can say 'give me my husband', so she would never return anything, which contradicts רבי יהודה

steps.title: Not an ordinary betrothed woman who sinned
steps.stepSummary: Maybe she is the betrothed of a regular ישראל and was with another man, so she can't say 'give me my husband'. If she did it willingly, she gets no כתובה. If she was forced, she is still allowed to him, so she could still say 'give me my husband'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe it is the wife of a ישראל who was with another man. In what way? If willingly, does she get a כתובה? If by force, she is still permitted to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third option: a woman who can't claim 'give me my husband' because she became forbidden to him. Both versions of this case fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא needs a woman who cannot say 'give me my husband' but still collects a כתובה. A willing sinner loses her כתובה. A woman who was forced is not forbidden to a regular ישראל, so the claim 'give me my husband' comes right back.

keyTerms.meaning: The betrothed wife of a regular (non-כהן) Jew
Willingly
By force, against her will
She is fully permitted to him

phrases.english: Rather, it is about the wife of an Israelite who committed adultery.
phrases.notes: Wife here means his betrothed, before the wedding.

phrases.english: And in what way? If willingly,
does she have a ketubah?
Rather, by force,
she is permitted to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third suggestion, looking for a woman who can't claim 'give me my husband'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both forms of the ordinary betrothed woman who was with another man
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Willingly: she has no כתובה. By force: she is still permitted, so she can claim 'give me my husband'

steps.title: The answer: a כהן's betrothed who was forced
steps.stepSummary: The case is a כהן's betrothed who was forced. She is forbidden to him, so she can't say 'give me my husband', but she still has a כתובה. The תנאים argue whether קידושין money is given to be kept for good. רבי מאיר says yes, רבי יהודה says no, and רבי יוסי is unsure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is the wife of a כהן who was forced. They argue about whether קידושין money is given to be kept for good. רבי מאיר holds it is given to be kept for good. רבי יהודה holds it is not. רבי יוסי is unsure whether it is or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally finds the case that fits the ברייתא and explains what the three תנאים are really arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who is forced becomes forbidden to a כהן. So she cannot say 'give me my husband', yet she keeps her כתובה because it was not her fault. Now the only question is whether קידושין money is a gift that stays with her no matter what. This is the same question as in step 8, which is why the גמרא called these 'the same תנאים'.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן's betrothed who was forced, and is now forbidden to him
קידושין money is given to be kept for good, like something sunk
They argue about
He is unsure

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the question 'is קידושין money kept for good?' only matters when she cannot say 'give me my husband' but still has a כתובה. A כהן's betrothed who was forced is exactly that case.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about the wife of a priest who was raped,
phrases.notes: Even when it is forced, she becomes forbidden to a כהן. So she can't say 'give me my husband', but she keeps her כתובה.

phrases.english: and they disagree about whether betrothal money is given as a sunk cost:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: קִדּוּשִׁין לְטִיבּוּעִין נִיתְּנוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds: betrothal money is given as a sunk cost,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: לָאו לְטִיבּוּעִין נִיתְּנוּ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda holds: it is not given as a sunk cost.
And Rabbi Yosei is uncertain
whether it is given as a sunk cost or not,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the case that survives after all earlier suggestions were rejected
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case the ברייתא is about
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כהן's betrothed who was forced; the dispute is whether קידושין money is kept for good

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי splits the money
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי יוסי is unsure, he splits the קידושין money in half. She owes back half, and that half is subtracted from the כתובה he owes her. That is why he gives her 30 half-סלעים when he betrothed her with 20 סלעים, and 20 half-סלעים when he betrothed her with 30.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, if he betrothed her with 20, he gives her 30 halves. If he betrothed her with 30, he gives her 20 halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי יוסי's numbers, now to explain them using his doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 20 סלעים are 80 דינרים, and half of that, 40, goes back to him. Her כתובה is 100, so he still owes her 60, which is 30 half-סלעים. With 30 סלעים, 120 דינרים, she owes back 60, so he still owes her 40, which is 20 half-סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: And therefore
A coin worth four דינרים; a 'half' is two דינרים

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: קידושין money is kept for good. רבי יהודה: it is not. רבי יוסי: unsure, so split it in half. The case is a כהן's betrothed who was forced, who cannot say 'give me my husband' but keeps her כתובה.

phrases.english: And therefore, if he betrothed her with twenty,
phrases.notes: Twenty סלעים, which are 80 דינרים. Half of it goes back to him and comes off the 100 of the כתובה.

phrases.english: he gives her thirty halves.
If he betrothed her with thirty,
he gives her twenty halves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכָּךְ קִדְּשָׁהּ בְּעֶשְׂרִים נוֹתֵן לָהּ שְׁלֹשִׁים חֲצָאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יוסי's doubt from step 15 to explain his numbers from step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since רבי יוסי is unsure whether קידושין money is kept for good, half is treated as returned and is subtracted from her כתובה.

steps.title: Local custom decides whether betrothal money is returned
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that wherever the custom is to return the קידושין money, it is returned. The גמרא explains that he was talking about the city of נהרדעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: Any place where people are used to giving back the betrothal money, they give it back. And we explain this as referring to נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the ברייתא to practical הלכה. רב נחמן says that local custom decides whether קידושין money is returned when the marriage does not go through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the תנאים argued about the money in theory. רב נחמן makes it practical: follow the local custom. The גמרא then pins down which place he meant, נהרדעא, where the custom was to return it.

keyTerms.meaning: they were used to, it was their custom
they give back
the explanation, how we read it
נהרדעא, a major Jewish city in בבל

phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said
Rav Naḥman said:
In every place where they were accustomed to return
phrases.notes: He means returning the קידושין money when the marriage falls apart.

phrases.english: they return it.
And the explanation: Neharde'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תנאים's argument to a practical ruling based on custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where the custom is to return קידושין money, it is returned; this refers to נהרדעא.

steps.title: What is the rule in the rest of Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the rule is in the other places in בבל, outside נהרדעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the rest of בבל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next answer: what happens in places that do not have נהרדעא's custom?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's rule only covered a place with a known custom. This question opens the case of places where the rule must be decided some other way.

keyTerms.meaning: the rest of בבל
what (is the rule)?

phrases.english: The rest of Babylonia, what is the rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about places not covered by the נהרדעא custom.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the rule about returning money in the rest of בבל?

steps.title: Gifts are returned, betrothal money is not
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף both say that in the rest of בבל the gifts are returned, but the קידושין money is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: The gifts are given back, but the betrothal money is not given back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: outside נהרדעא, the groom gets back his gifts but not the קידושין money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This separates two kinds of money. The gifts come back to him, but the קידושין money itself stays with her. רב פפא will refine this rule in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: gifts (given in connection with the marriage)
are returned
the betrothal money
both of them

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both say:
The gifts are returned,
the betrothal money is not returned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the rest of בבל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gifts are returned; קידושין money is not.

steps.title: The final ruling depends on who ended the marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules: if he died, she died, or he backed out, the gifts come back but not the קידושין money. If she backed out, even the קידושין money comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said, the הלכה is: Whether he died, or she died, or he changed his mind, the gifts are returned but the betrothal money is not. If she changed her mind, even the betrothal money is returned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the final הלכה and makes it depend on who caused the marriage to end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא keeps רבה and רב יוסף's basic rule for most cases. But he adds an exception: when she is the one who backs out, she must give back even the קידושין money, since the breakup is her doing.

keyTerms.meaning: the final הלכה
he changed his mind, backed out
she changed her mind, backed out

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא: if he died, she died, or he backed out, only the gifts come back. If she backed out, the קידושין money also comes back.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said, the halakha is:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁמֵּת הוּא, בֵּין שֶׁמֵּתָה הִיא,
phrases.english: whether he died, whether she died,
or he retracted,
the gifts are returned,
the betrothal money is not returned.
If she retracted,
even the betrothal money is also returned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבה and רב יוסף's rule and adds an exception when she backs out.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only gifts return unless she is the one who backs out, in which case the קידושין money returns too.

steps.title: Betrothal money is not returned, so people won't think he may marry her sister
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says the קידושין money is not returned. This is a rabbinic decree, so people won't think the קידושין never counted and that he can marry her sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: The betrothal money is not returned. This is a decree, so that people won't say that קידושין can take hold with her sister.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר disagrees with the last part of רב פפא's ruling. Even when she backs out, the קידושין money is not returned. He bases this on what people might wrongly conclude.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people see the קידושין money handed back, they may think the קידושין was canceled from the start. Then they would think he may marry her sister, which is really forbidden, since the קידושין did take hold.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake
lest people say
take hold, take effect
her sister

steps.confusionAlert: The decree is not saying the קידושין really failed. It did take hold; the worry is only that people would wrongly think it failed.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
The betrothal money is not returned,
a decree, lest they say
that betrothal takes effect with her sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רב פפא's exception in step 20 (that when she backs out even the קידושין money is returned), and gives a decree as the reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין money is not returned, as a decree so people won't think he may marry her sister.

steps.title: Her divorce document proves she was married
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says there is no worry, because her גט shows that she was truly married.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Her divorce document proves it about her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on אמימר's worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she needed a גט, everyone can see the קידושין was real. So, says רב אשי, nobody will think he may marry her sister, and there is no need for the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: her divorce document
proves, shows clearly

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Her bill of divorce proves it about her.
phrases.notes: He means the גט shows she was really betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: גִּיטָּהּ מוֹכִיחַ עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אמימר's reason for the decree.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אמימר's worry that people will think the קידושין failed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The גט already shows the קידושין was real.

steps.title: רב אשי's answer is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב אשי's answer is a mistake, because some people hear about the money being returned but never hear about the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this statement of רב אשי is a mistake, since there are people who heard about this but did not hear about that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's answer and so supports אמימר's decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט only helps people who know about it. Someone who only heard that the money was returned could still make the mistake, so אמימר's worry stands.

keyTerms.meaning: a mistake, a made-up idea
heard

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא backs אמימר: the קידושין money is not returned, because not everyone who hears about the money also hears about the גט.

phrases.english: And this of Rav Ashi is a mistake,
since there is one who heard about this
and did not hear about that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's rejection, so אמימר's decree stands.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אשי's claim that the גט removes the worry.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not everyone who hears about the returned money hears about the גט.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: groomsmen's gifts can be collected in court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: groomsmen's gifts can be collected through בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because groomsmen's gifts can be collected in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its reason about שושבינות, setting up a ברייתא that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said שושבינות gifts are returned to the middle (shared estate), because they are a real debt that בית דין can collect. Now the גמרא will explain what is special about these gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: gifts given by groomsmen at a wedding, to be repaid later
can be collected
court

phrases.english: Because gifts of groomsmen
are collectible in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by returning to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שושבינות is a debt that בית דין can collect.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists five rules about groomsmen's gifts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says there are five rules about שושבינות. It begins: they can be collected in court, they are repaid at the right time, and they have no problem of interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Five things were said about groomsmen's gifts: they can be collected in court, they are paid back at their proper time, and there is no problem of interest with them,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists five rules about שושבינות. The list starts here and continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule supports the משנה: these gifts are a real debt. The gift is only repaid at the proper time, meaning at the groomsman's own wedding. And repaying with a bigger gift is not forbidden interest.

keyTerms.meaning: is repaid at its proper time
interest, forbidden extra payment on a loan

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Five things were said about gifts of groomsmen:
they are collectible in court,
and they are returned at their time,
phrases.notes: The proper time is the groomsman's own wedding.

phrases.english: and they are not subject to the prohibition of interest,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּשׁוֹשְׁבִינוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that backs and expands the משנה's rule about שושבינות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שושבינות can be collected in court, is repaid at its proper time, and is not subject to interest (list continues).
